elements.name: Opening
elements.html:
Sponsor: AstraZeneca AB

Phase: 3

 

Opening

 

Thank you for your interest in our weight loss clinical trial. As you may or may not know, obesity is rapidly increasing as a worldwide concern due to its innate risk factor for other life-threatening conditions such as type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease or heart failure. As such, there is an ongoing and urgent need to achieve sustained weight loss. Therefore, this study will be assessing the safety and effectiveness of a new medication to support weight loss.

elements.name: Study Drug and Design
elements.html:
Study Drug and Design

 

The investigational product for this study is called Elecoglipron (E-LE-CO-GLI-PRON). It is an orally taken GLP-1 agonist, meaning it works similarly to some other weight loss drugs like Ozempic, by working on certain pathways to help suppress hunger and alter your metabolism to burn more energy.

 

The study involves 2 separate treatment periods. For the first, you're placed into one of 3 groups, and for the second, the groups are split once more to become 6 groups in total. Some participants will receive the study drug for both treatment periods, and some will receive it for one treatment period and a placebo for the other. Thus, regardless of which group you're in, everyone will receive the study drug at some point in time.

 

This study is double-blinded, meaning neither you nor the study doctors will know the group you're in until the end of the study. This ensures a lack of bias and stronger reliability.

 

Screening time: 3.5h

 

(If PT wants more detail about the 6 groups and the allocation, go to the bottom of the page for additional information)

elements.name: Study Duration
elements.html:
Study Duration
 

This study goes on for about 2.5 years and there are 22 visits. I know that sounds like a large commitment, but the visits are spread out, and so you don't have to come in super frequently. 

 

Treatment period 1 is 72 weeks, and treatment period 2 is 52 weeks:

 

  • Screening visit
  • Treatment period 1:
    • Visit every 4 weeks from week 0-24
      • Phone call halfway between each visit
    • Visit every 12 weeks from week 24-72
      • Phone call every 4 weeks from week 28-68
  • Treatment period 2:
    • Visit every 4 weeks from week 72-96
      • Phone call halfway between each visit
    • Visit every 12 weeks from week 96-124
      • Phone call every 4 weeks from week 100-120
    • Last visit at week 126

 

These visits include treatment titration (working you up to the desired dosage slowly so that you adapt well), and a variety of tests to see how you are doing and how the drug is affecting you. These include lab tests, like bloods and urine tests, and for some people, DEXA scans or diabetes checks like retinal fundus photography (pictures of the eyes).

 

There are also windows of leniency around when these visits will occur, meaning if you can't make it on the exact day, you can come in a few days earlier or later.

elements.name: Reimbursement
elements.html:
Reimbursement

 

You will be reimbursed the following for any reasonable travel, parking, meals, and other expenses associated with your study visits: 

  • $100 for Screening, Visit 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 19, 20 and 22
  • $125 for Visit 2, 8, 10, 12, 18 and 21
  • $50 for each scheduled phone call

 

This means if you attend all scheduled visits, you can receive up to $2650.

 

If you're eligible for extra reimbursement related to rural travel, the study team will let you know.

elements.name: Disclosure
elements.html:
Disclosure

 

Before we go any further, I want to explain exactly how the reimbursement works, so there are no surprises for you later. The reimbursement I just went through is what you'd receive if everything goes ahead as planned. That can look a bit different depending on what happens on the day. For example, if the doctor looks over your information early on and finds you're not eligible before you even get to the consent form, if you decide not to sign the consent form yourself, or if something doesn't line up with what you've told me today, you'd likely only get a partial amount, or in some cases nothing, instead of the full reimbursement.

 

That's actually a big part of why it matters that you're as accurate as possible with me right now. The doctor's early review is based on exactly what you tell me today, so the more accurate you are, the better your chances of making it all the way through screening and getting the full reimbursement.

elements.name: Additional notes
elements.html:
Additional study details if PT wants them

 

The study involves 2 separate treatment periods. For the first, you will be randomly placed into one of 3 groups and have an equal chance of being in any of the 3:

 

Group 1 - Low dose of Elecoglipron (45mg)

Group 2 - High dose of Elecoglipron (65mg)

Group 3 - Placebo

 

After treatment period 1, you will be randomly placed into a group once more for treatment period 2. Each group of the first period will split further into two groups. If you're in group 1 or 2 for the first period, you have a ⅔ chance of continuing on your dosage and a ⅓ chance of being put on the placebo for the second period. If you're in the placebo group in the first period, you have a 50% chance of receiving either a low or high dose for the second period.

 

Your overall chances of each combination are as follows:

 

Group 1a - Low dose + Low dose = 2/9 (22.22%)

Group 1b - Low dose + Placebo = 1/9 (11.11%)
 

Group 2a - High dose + High dose = 2/9 (22.22%)

Group 2b - High dose + Placebo = 1/9 (11.11%)
 

Group 3a - Placebo + low dose = 1/6 (16.67%)

Group 3b - Placebo + high dose = 1/6 (16.67%)

elements.name: BW Stable
elements.title: Has your weight been stable for the last 90 days (no fluctuations beyond 5% either way)?

elements.name: BW Stability Ex
elements.html:
Example for the 5% rule:

 

Starting weight: 70 kg

  • 5% weight change = 3.5 kg

     

    • More than 5% weight change (not allowed):
      • Weight loss of 4 kg → New weight: 66 kg (5.71% loss)

      • Weight gain of 4.5 kg → New weight: 74.5 kg (6.43% gain)

         

    • Less than 5% weight change (allowed):
      • Weight loss of 2.5 kg → New weight: 67.5 kg (3.57% loss)

      • Weight gain of 2 kg → New weight: 72 kg (2.86% gain)

         

For this example, changes greater than 3.5 kg (either loss or gain) are not allowed, while changes less than 3.5 kg are acceptable.

 

Please keep in mind that these values change according to the starting weight! For example, for a person who weighs 120kg, a 5% weight change would be 6kg.

elements.name: Liver Problems Info
elements.html:
Cirrhosis (si-ro-sis) = permanent scarring and stiffeninf of the liver, usually due to chronic liver disease

 

Ascites (Uh-sigh-teez) - Abnormal buildup of excess fluid in abdominal cavity (usually caused by cirrhosis)

 

Encephalopathy (En-se-fa-lo-path-ee) - Decline in brain function due to chronic liver disease

 

Variceal (Va-ri-see-uhl) bleeding - Enlarged, fragile veins rupture and bleed due to cirrhosis

 

“Liver disease” includes alcoholic/drug-induced/viral/autoimmune hepatitis, fatty liver disease, bile duct scarring/inflammation, liver damage caused by iron overload, alpha 1 antitrypsin deficiency, and Wilson's disease.

elements.name: Arrhythmia Info
elements.html:
See what best fits their description:

 

Atrioventricular block - Electrical signals from the atria (upper chambers) to the ventricles (lower chambers) are delayed/blocked

 

Sinus node dysfunction - Heart's natural pacemaker not able to keep its required rhythm

 

Ventricular arrhythmia - Abnormal heart rhythms originating in the ventricles (heart's lower chambers)

 

Atrial fibrillation/flutter - Abnormal rhythm in the atria (heart's upper chambers)

elements.name: Exclusionary Meds Summary
elements.html:
Command + F to make sure we haven't missed anything exclusionary. Also Command + F on previous page.

 

Reminder, exclusionary medications include:

  • Changes in last year to drug doses associated with weight gain (Amitriptyline, Nortriptyline, Carbamazepine, Olanzapine, Chlorpromazine Paroxetine, Clozapine, Perphenazine, Doxepin, Phenelzine, Fluoxetine, Quetiapine, Fluvoxamine, Risperidone, Gabapentin, Sertraline, Haloperidol, Thioridazine, Imipramine, Tranylcypromine, Lithium, Trimipramine, Mirtazapine, Valproic acid and its derivatives)

  • Recent systemic long-term glucocorticoid use (longer than 14 days consecutively in the last 90 days)
  • Current use of the following prohibited medication:
    • Carbamazepine, Phenytoin (anticonvulsants/analgesics)
    • Itraconazole, Ketoconazole, Clotrimazole, Fluconazole (oral/injectable antifungals)
    • Clarithromycin, Rifampin, oral/injectable Ciprofloxacin, oral/injectable Erythromycin, Quinine (anti-infectives)
    • Antivirals for Hep C
    • Diltiazem, Verapamil, Felodipine (calcium channel blockers)
    • Cimetidine (H2-blockers)
    • Ticagrelor (anti-platelet medication)
    • Buspirone, Quetiapine, Triazolam (anxiolytics/antidepressants/antipsychotics)
    • Budesonide (oral/injectable glucocorticoids)
    • Quinidine, Digoxin (anti-arrhythmics)
    • Colchicine (antigout medication)
    • Cyclosporine, Sirolimus, Tacrolimus (oral/injectable immunosuppressives)
    • Sildenafil (phosphodiesterase inhibitors)
    • Pioglitazone, Repaglinide, Rosiglitazone (glucose-lowering medication)
    • Prazosin (antihypertensives)
    • Sulfasalazine (anti-inflammatory medication)
    • Sulphonylureases
      • Glimepiride (Amaryl)
      • Glipizide (Glucotrol, Glucotrol XL)
      • Glyburide / Glibenclamide (DiaBeta, Glynase)
    • Thiazolidinediones

choices.text: Postmenopausal, with cessation of menses for at least 12 months - Continue ✅

elements.name: Infertility Info
elements.html:
“Infertility due to surgery” refers to:

  • Hysterectomy - Removal of uterus
  • Bilateral oophorectomy - Removal of both ovaries
  • Bilateral salpingectomy - Removal of both Fallopian tubes

 

"Permanent infertility due to alternate medical cause" includes things like:

  • Mullerian agenesis - Improper development of uterus and cervix from birth
  • Gonadal dysgenesis - Improper development of ovaries from birth

 

If a PT has something like this, it will likely be a doctor's enquiry. Check with TL and TST too though.

elements.name: COCP Info
elements.html:
“Combined” = oestrogen + progestogen

Ask for the brand and dosage, and raise Dr enquiry

 

Ethinyl oestradiol (e-thin-il ee-stra-die-ol) dose is most important. Must be ≤ 20 micrograms, but regardless of dose, raise enquiry with all these details please.`

elements.name: Male Double Barrier
elements.title: This study requires male participants to use a condom whenever engaging in sexual activity with the opposite sex, and female sexual partners should also be using a highly effective form of contraception if they are not menopausal or medically unable to have children. Is this OK?
elements.description:
Menopausal = no menses for 12 months+

Medically unable = hysterectomy, bilateral oopherectomy, bilateral salpingectomy

Highly effective = IUD, IUS, the pill, minipill, implanon, biltareal tubal occlusion, male partner vasectomised

elements.name: Referral Q
elements.title: Before we wrap up, I’d like to share details about our referral program. If you refer someone to us you can receive up to $250 if they enrol and participate in the study. Would you like to hear more?

elements.name: Referral Info
elements.html:
Great! Here's how it works:

 

To refer someone, you will need to provide them with a unique referral ID. The person you refer will need to provide us this ID either when they sign up on our website, or when they speak to us over the phone. This ID is essential, as it ensures we can track and reimburse you for any referrals.

 

For each person you refer who comes in for an in-person screening visit, you'll receive $50. If they go on to enrol and participate in the study, you'll earn an additional $200.

 

There's no limit- you can refer as many people as you'd like, as long as you have an exisiting relationship with them. It's important to note that you cannot advertise for referrals. This program is based on personal connections, so please only refer people you know.

 

If you're interested, we can set up your Unique Referral ID today if you would like (the unique referral ID is REF[p number]. E.g., REFP14471)

 

Who do you know you might be interested in this trial? (if they don't know anyone for this trial, they can also refer someone to any other trial)

 

Would you like us to send you an email that you can forward on to them?
